data.raw_text:
The cost of a newly opened government health center in Pasig City has drawn comparisons to delayed and more costly public works, showing that taxpayers value how their funds are spent.

The Pasig City government inaugurated the E. Santos Health Center on February 27, a three-storey complex complete with CCTV monitoring, fire safety systems, and patient facilities. The structure replaced an older facility within the same complex, which city officials said was “not ideal” and did not have sufficient space or facilities.

The project cost ₱13.5 million and was constructed from March to November 2025, which netizens praised for its cost efficiency. Many drew comparisons to other government projects that cost more and took longer to complete, yet ended up dysfunctional.

For instance, some cited the city-sponsored ₱300-million waiting sheds along Commonwealth Avenue in Quezon City, which have yet to be completed and reportedly fail to protect commuters from rain and heat due to their design. Others recalled a nearly ₱10-million one-storey multipurpose hall with solar panels in Bacoor, Cavite measuring only 80 square meters, which took more than a year to complete.

The widespread comparisons highlight the role of social media in shaping accountability in governance: when taxpayers compare notes on how their local governments handle projects and deliver services, the pressure is on for elected officials to deliver.

Report by Kiara Gorrospe

#radarPHBusiness #radarPH
